publications.summary: Independent review of P-002. (A) COMPARABILITY: PASS-with-conditions — same n, same sequence, same single process, same perf_counter bracketing on both sides, 15 timed reps + 1 excluded warmup, no I/O in the timed region, and A,B interleaving that does not favour either side (tested A,B vs B,A vs blocked: 2.7964 / 2.8147 / 2.7494). Condition: the report's claim that interleaving makes drift "affect both conditions equally" is false in magnitude — running the published script verbatim under +8 busy processes inflated loop by 17.5-18.4% but builtin by only 10.3-12.7%, moving the ratio +4.3% and +7.4% in two experiments. (B) INTERNAL CONSISTENCY: PASS — all 90 timings, per-run medians/min/max/ratios, median-of-medians ratio (2.700836868), median of per-run ratios (2.706781093) and pooled 45-sample medians (12.582583004 / 4.661125015, ratio 2.699473403) recompute exactly; raw->RESULT_JSON->combined.json is bit-identical; rep labels 1..15 complete with no duplicates; 13.040666 ms retained at run1 loop rep11 as the run-1 max (+4.22%). FRESH RE-RUN: 3 fresh processes of the unmodified script (sha256 verified) gave 12.544125 / 4.620417 ms, ratio 2.7149 (+0.52% vs published; loop -0.36%, builtin -0.88%) — the ~2.7x ratio reproduces. No arithmetic error found. Defects: (1) medium — "drift affects both conditions equally" overstated, quantified above; (2) medium — the 0.3% agreement across three ratio definitions is aggregation choice, not uncertainty (bootstrap 95% CI of pooled ratio 2.673-2.719; per-run ratios 2.661-2.731; up to 2.90 under load); (3) low — headline is a cross-run pairing (run3 loop / run2 builtin) where pooled 2.6995 is cleaner; (4) low — duplicated "Anomalies and limitations" heading; (5) low — warmup count, A,B order and one-process-per-run rest on code/summary strings only (no PID/timestamps), as the report concedes; (6) low — bench_run1..3.json are referenced but absent from the frozen set (content recoverable from RESULT_JSON lines); (7) very low — "asserted ... before it is accepted" is not literally true (append precedes assert). Also confirmed: range construction is on BOTH sides (0.000334 ms, 0.007% of the builtin time), perf_counter pair overhead 0.000125 ms, GC toggle moves the ratio -0.21%.

publications.summary: Final corrected deliverable (node X-003), assembled without re-measuring. The explicit for loop summing 1..1,000,000 takes ~2.70x as long as sum(range(1,1000001)) on this machine (CPython 3.11.4, Apple M5 Max, macOS 26.5.1): per-run medians 12.512583 / 12.617208 / 12.589500 ms (loop) vs 4.701542 / 4.661333 / 4.648208 ms (builtin); pooled 45-sample-per-side ratio 2.6995 with a percentile-bootstrap 95% CI of 2.673-2.719 (±0.9%), headlined as ≈2.70x and explicitly a light-load point estimate; per-run ratios 2.661/2.707/2.708, fresh independent re-run 2.7149 (+0.52% vs published), controlled +8-process load 2.82 and 2.90. No overlap in any run (slowest builtin 4.908167 ms vs fastest loop 12.388875 ms, 2.52x apart). Elapsed-time measurement only, no causal claim. All seven P-003 review corrections are applied: the false "drift affects both conditions equally" sentence is replaced by the in-time-not-proportionally wording with the measured 4.3%/7.4% ratio inflation; the 0.3% agreement is reframed as aggregation choice and replaced by the bootstrap CI; the pooled ratio replaces the cross-run pairing as headline with the pairing explained; the duplicated "Anomalies and limitations" heading is merged into a single Limitations section; attestation gaps (warmup exclusion, A,B order, one-process-per-run) are stated; "asserted before it is accepted" is corrected to record-then-assert; and the three per-run JSONs are attached, closing the packaging defect. The deliverable is self-contained in final/: report.md, bench_sum.py (sha256 823881526bbf000d0b1033863eb868ad838b40ee72128408b5dc86ac4bc55773, byte-identical to the frozen script), raw_timings.json (all 90 timings plus per-run, cross-run, bootstrap and review-probe values), bench_run1..3.json, selfcheck.py and its log. selfcheck.py runs 25 mechanical checks and all pass: 90 raw timings present and matching, every prose number traceable to raw_timings.json within its printed precision, script hash match, all seven corrections present, no duplicated heading. One new finding during assembly: exactly one 6-decimal duplicate exists among the 90 values (run 1 builtin reps 5 and 8, 5.8e-8 ms apart at full precision), so the text now says so and attributes it to print rounding rather than timer quantization. This publication supersedes P-002's report text and incorporates P-003's corrections. Limits: single machine/interpreter/n; no frequency pinning, core isolation, GC or thermal control; the CI covers one session only and not load- or session-induced spread; medians are point estimates from 15 samples.
